subject.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue

question: Should aged lower-priority command queue entries be allowed to overtake fresh foreground/user work, or should foreground dominance remain absolute?
rationale: Both choices are defensible scheduler policies, but the current branch mixes the stronger anti-starvation claim with foreground-preserving implementation.

options.title: Match the anti-starvation contract
options.body: Let aged low-priority entries promote above fresh foreground after the threshold, then update tests and proof to match the canonical issue.

options.title: Keep foreground absolute
options.body: Rename and narrow the PR so it no longer claims to prevent steady-foreground starvation, and track strict anti-starvation elsewhere.

options.title: Pause for broader scheduler work
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers want one combined policy with the foreground-reserve and fairness work.

recommendation.title: Match the anti-starvation contract
recommendation.body: Let aged low-priority entries promote above fresh foreground after the threshold, then update tests and proof to match the canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He has both original queue history and an overlapping scheduler proposal, making him the best available owner for the policy choice.
